flags: The 2013 tourism page contradicts itself on waterfall heights (114/65 feet in captions, 110/85 feet in body); Wikipedia qualifies Upper Mesa’s 114 feet as roughly. Heights omitted. The current material’s claim that both falls are ten stories high is not used.
Use 28.2 miles and 49 minutes from the April 2026 tourism capture; older tourism text gives 28.7 miles and one hour. These are source estimates, not a timed drive.

North-to-south order follows strip-map mileage ending at Ashton, reversing the current story’s direction. All three moment titles, existing coordinates and waterfall-cove motifs retained; no coordinates added for Upper Mesa Falls.

Cache documents stage-stop and overlook history but no highway construction or designation campaign. Formal state/National Forest designation tiers are not explicitly established in the cached route text.
Lower Mesa Falls and Warm River moments are shorter than 90 words because focused evidence is thin. No businesses substituted for landmarks.
Winter closure is supported by the April 2026 archived tourism page. Checked date records cache review; no live road status or seasonal opening dates available.
The 2013 claim that these are Idaho’s only major falls not used for irrigation or power is omitted because no current managing or scientific source in the cache verifies that statewide superlative.
